2.text: and the Kamchadal, on the contrary, during a night passed in the open, have

3.text: a cheerful fire, and protect themselves with heavy double overcoats and sleeping-

4.text: bags made of thick skins. The Chukchee seldom use fawn-skins for their

5.text: overcoats, because the hair and skin are not sufficiently tough and durable.

6.text: Summer skins of full-grown reindeer, with their short slick hair, are most

7.text: suitable. Thicker skins, employed for this purpose, have their hair previously

8.text: cropped short. They are worn with the hairy side in. The outside is usually

9.text: dyed yellow with ochre, or dark red with alder-bark.

10.text: Chukchee overcoats are made in the form of long ample frocks reaching

11.text: far below the knees, with a loose hood, and very full sleeves gathered at the

12.text: wrists. The lower edge is often bordered with narrow strips of fur or leather.

13.text: Near the edge the overcoat is trimmed with a band of leather, usually of

14.text: different color, the reverse side of the skin being turned out.

15.text: The overcoats of the southwestern tribes are trimmed along the lower

16.text: edge with much broader strips of cotton or cloth of bright colors, — white,

17.text: red, or blue. These are embroidered in various designs.

18.text: The belt is made of a piece of tough leather, with a clasp of ivory or of

19.text: iron. It is sometimes rudely adorned with buttons, bells, or other jingling

20.text: objects. Fig. 176 represents a Chukchee belt with a big iron clasp. Strips
